steps.what: 8b. DEATH (the Escape strip's sibling): Creature.RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath strips every power whose ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath() is true -- the C# DEFAULT -- and awaits each one's AfterRemoved; the sim strips nothing, ever
steps.issue: ADDED 2026-07-26 in the power tier's review fix pass. Until then this engine-wide absence existed only as prose (.superpowers/sdd/content-power-report-b.md section 3c) and carried no verdict anywhere, so it reached neither audit_status nor the gap queue nor any fix work list. C# SIDE: on the real-death branch CreatureCmd.cs:533-537 calls `creature.RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath()` and then awaits `item.AfterRemoved(creature)` for each power it returns -- the deliberate contrast with escape (step 8), which strips SILENTLY. Creature.cs:668-671 defines it as `RemoveAllPowersInternalExcept(_powers.Where(p => !p.ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath() || !Hook.ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath(p)))`, i.e. STRIP BY DEFAULT: PowerModel.ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath's base implementation returns **true** (PowerModel.cs:637-640 -- "Usually true, but false for powers that do things like revive their owner"), only six non-mock powers override it (AdaptablePower.cs:67, DieForYouPower.cs:49, MinionPower.cs:15, PainfulStabsPower.cs:24, ReattachPower.cs:98, SteamEruptionPower.cs:37), and Hook.ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath (Hook.cs:2495-2509) has exactly one implementer in the entire decompiled game (IllusionPower.cs:59-66). SIM SIDE: cmds.py:96-105 goes straight from the HP write to should_die / should_remove_from_combat_after_death / on_death. There is no strip, no AfterRemoved analogue and no `should_power_be_removed_on_death` dispatcher in hooks.py; a grep of sts2_rl for a death-time `powers.clear()` or per-power removal returns nothing. The sim therefore INVERTS THE DEFAULT: every power C# strips survives. **LIVE, executed 2026-07-26** on the Decimillipede: a DecimillipedeSegmentFront given Vulnerable 3 and then hit for 999 ends at hp 0, is_dead True, retained_after_death True and still holding ['reattach', 'vulnerable']; `ReattachPower.do_reattach()` (powers.py:2359-2367) brings it back at 25 HP still Vulnerable 3. In the game the same segment loses the Vulnerable on death -- VulnerablePower does not override ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath, ReattachPower overrides only its own (ReattachPower.cs:98) and implements no ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath, so nothing vetoes the strip. The Decimillipede is a ported Hive elite (monsters/hive/decimillipede.py, monsters/hive/__init__.py:63) and Bash/Vulnerable is ported basic-pool Ironclad content. Second-order: this absence is why several ported powers hand-roll their own `_expire()` where C# adds none -- the sim compensating for the missing strip one power at a time. CROSS-REFERENCED BY (rule 3, one verdict per mechanism at every site): power/adaptable, power/minion, power/painful_stabs, power/reattach and power/steam_eruption, whose OWN ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath overrides stay `faithful` because they ask for exactly the behaviour the sim gives for free; and power/illusion, which owns the Hook.ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath half of the predicate. SOURCE PINNING: CreatureCmd.cs, Creature.cs and Hook.cs are already in this record's hashed game_sources, and cmds.py in its sim_sources. PowerModel.cs:637-640 is a third-file citation here, hashed by audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json, so drift is still detected; adding it to this record's source set would mean editing harness.py's SEAM_SOURCES table, which is outside this fix pass's scope.

Five non-mock powers override it, and all five are ported: AdaptablePower.cs:53-56, InfestedPower, SteamEruptionPower.cs:23-26, StockPower, SurprisePower. The mechanism already carries `gap` at its five per-power sites (power/adaptable, power/infested, power/steam_eruption, power/stock, power/surprise); this step is its engine-level home, same verdict per rule 3. steps.what: 13. Hook.ModifyBlock: enchantment additive/multiplicative FIRST, then a per-listener additive chain, then a per-listener multiplicative chain -- both loops threading the RUNNING decimal (num += / num *=); NO pipeline-level props gate
steps.issue: See guard G1 (LIVE). Two divergences in one step: (a) BlockCmd.apply (cmds.py:145-147) skips the entire dispatch unless is_powered_attack(props), while Hook.ModifyBlock (Hook.cs:1310-1340) calls every listener for every block gain -- and Vambrace.cs:59-63 / PaelsLegion.cs:132-134 self-gate only on IsCardOrMonsterMove() (Move alone); (b) C# applies the source card's own enchantment modifiers before any listener (Hook.cs:1314-1319), whereas the sim's enchantments are ordinary modify_block_additive listeners (enchantments.py:298, 428) ordered only by registration -- and are additionally skipped by the same (a) gate. (c) AGGREGATION SHAPE -- this is gap G9 of audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json (step 31), the same mechanism as audit/records/seam/damage_pipeline.json guard N3, carried here at the third and last of its three sites (rule 3: one verdict per mechanism at every site, including across records). NOTE ON NAMING: "G9" here always means hook_dispatch's G9; this record's own guard G9 (ShouldDraw) is unrelated. CONFIRMED, not assumed: Hook.ModifyBlock (Hook.cs:1320-1337) has EXACTLY the shape of Hook.ModifyDamageInternal (Hook.cs:2515-2538) -- two sequential foreach loops over IterateCombatHookListeners, `decimal num2 = item.ModifyBlockAdditive(target, num, ...); num += num2;` (1322-1323) then `decimal num3 = item2.ModifyBlockMultiplicative(target, num, ...); num *= num3;` (1331-1332), each contribution folded into the running decimal immediately and the next listener handed the folded value -- and the sim has EXACTLY the damage site's parallel shape: hooks.py:98-109 sums every listener's additive return against the same pre-step base and hooks.py:111-122 multiplies every listener's factor together in FLOAT, after which cmds.py:145-147 applies each aggregate once (`amount = amount + hooks.modify_block_additive(...)` then `amount = int(amount * hooks.modify_block_multiplicative(...))`). Same divergence, same verdict: gap. DORMANT at the block site (the damage site is LIVE), evidence executed, in three parts. (1) The base-vs-running ARGUMENT is inert here too: `py audit/tools/dormancy_probes.py cs-running-value` finds 0 of 46 C# Modify{Damage,Block}{Additive,Multiplicative} overrides reading the value they are handed -- 10 of those 46 are the block pair (2 ModifyBlockAdditive: DexterityPower.cs:20, FastenPower.cs:20; 8 ModifyBlockMultiplicative: FrailPower.cs:22, NoBlockPower.cs:30, ShadowmeldPower.cs:24, UnmovablePower.cs:21, PaelsLegion.cs:134, Vambrace.cs:57, VitruvianMinion.cs:34, MultiplayerScalingModel.cs:52) -- and `sim-running-value` finds 0 of 31 sim implementations reading theirs. (2) The block ADDITIVE family is therefore exactly equal, `base + sum(a_i) == the sequential fold` over integers. (3) The block MULTIPLICATIVE family, unlike damage's, is ALSO equal today, because every reachable block factor is BINARY-EXACT (dyadic) and a float product of dyadic factors equals the sequential decimal fold bit for bit. An AST enumeration of sts2_rl finds exactly five ported implementations -- Frail x0.75 (powers.py:452), Unmovable x2.0 (powers.py:1105), No Block x0.0 (powers.py:3673), Pael's Legion x2.0 (relics/paels_legion.py:36), Vambrace x2.0 (relics/vambrace.py:26) -- factor set {0.0, 0.75, 2.0}; an exhaustive sweep of all 15 ordered subsets of that set x bases 0..999 finds 0 mismatches between int(base * product) (sim), the sequential decimal fold (game) and a sequential-float control. Executed end-to-end through the real pipeline: a player holding the ported Vambrace with 1 Frail gaining 5 card block gets 7 in the sim and 7 in the game (game 5m x 2m = 10m, 10m x 0.75m = 7.5m, Creature.cs:459-466 GainBlockInternal truncates to 7; sim 2.0 * 0.75 == 1.5 exactly, int(5 * 1.5) == 7), where the damage site's Shrink x0.7 + Vulnerable x1.5 gives 20 vs 21. CONCRETE TRIGGER: any block multiplier whose factor is not binary-exact. None exists in single-player content -- all 8 C# ModifyBlockMultiplicative overrides return dyadic values (FrailPower.cs:32 0.75m, NoBlockPower.cs:44 0m, ShadowmeldPower.cs:30 2^Amount, UnmovablePower.cs:40 2m, PaelsLegion.cs:152 2m, Vambrace.cs:79 2m, VitruvianMinion.cs:48 2m) and the ONLY non-dyadic block factor anywhere in the decompiled source is MultiplayerScalingModel.cs:52-68 (playerCount x {1.1m, 1.2m, 1.3m}), which hook_dispatch's note N1 waives as multiplayer. So the named unported thing that would make this site live is a block multiplier returning a non-dyadic factor -- concretely, a port of the MultiplayerScalingModel factor, or any new content mirroring the damage side's x0.7 Shrink shape onto block. NOT pinned by a test for exactly that reason: with today's ported content the two shapes cannot be made to disagree, so a strict xfail would XPASS. The damage site's pin, test/test_hook_order.py::TestHookDispatchOrder::test_multiplicative_damage_modifiers_chain_sequentially, is the mechanism's one pin.

guards.what: G7 (dormant) -- ExhaustCmd.exhaust only knows about the hand and the discard pile
guards.issue: cmds.py:379-384 removes the card from `hand` or `discard_pile` and appends it to `exhaust_pile`; a card in the draw pile, the exhaust pile, or mid-play stays where it is AND lands in the exhaust pile, i.e. it exists in two piles at once. C# routes through CardPileCmd.Add(card, PileType.Exhaust, Bottom), whose RemoveFromCurrentPile() is pile-agnostic (CardPileCmd.cs:496) and whose CardPile.AddInternal throws outright if the target pile already holds the instance (CardPile.cs:86-89) -- so BOTH observed states are exceptions in the game. Dormant: all twelve ported callers pass hand cards (spot-checked cards/cinder.py:40-45, cards/true_grit.py:48-54, cards/second_wind.py:34-39, relics/paels_eye.py:44-46). The sim has no modify_shuffle_order hook at all: PerfectFitEnchantment hand-rolls the reposition on on_shuffle (enchantments.py:186-189), i.e. on the AfterShuffle event, so the net order is decided by hook-REGISTRATION order rather than by C#'s fixed call sequence. (3) The initial-shuffle variant has no sim surface at all: wrapping the hook system across `_shuffle_draw_pile(stable=False)` records ZERO hook invocations. guards.what: G11 (dormant) -- AfterCardDiscarded fires before the card has moved, and in a batch
guards.issue: C# adds each card to the discard pile FIRST and only then fires the hook, one card at a time, so the next card is not moved until the previous card's hook has run (CardCmd.cs:186-195).
